clue.text: Couch potato needs sex partner and a wrestling match

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
a bout is a single contest in wrestling or boxing

explanation.surface: A lazy sofa-dweller is told he needs a lover and a spot of wrestling to liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is an idle person who does nothing, just as a couch potato lounges in front of the television.

clue.text: Thieving Ronnie, the board member

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ronnie ..., a London robber of the 1980s, once married to Barbara Windsor
second meaning: the chess piece shaped like a horse

explanation.surface: A light-fingered Ronnie turns out to be sitting on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board member' suggests a company director; it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece is called a knight, and the criminal's surname was Knight, so one word covers both.

clue.text: On a trip, Stephen was so done in

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was killed by stoning

explanation.surface: Someone called Stephen got wrecked while away on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a drunken holiday; the second half is about the martyr in the Book of Acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for intoxicated on drugs, and also means killed by having rocks thrown at you.

clue.text: Rock: vivacious and witty type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rock is slang for a diamond
second meaning: a lively, brilliant person

explanation.surface: A rock star described as lively and witty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkler is slang for a diamond, and figuratively a person who shines in company.

clue.text: Homosexual grabbing sex around English theatre once

indicators.note: the outer word clutches the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: gay means homosexual

indicators.note: the word for sex wraps itself round the letter for English

parts.note: it is a crossword standard for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A gay man grabs some sex somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gaiety was a famous London theatre on the Strand, now gone, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaiety Theatre in London's West End was a music-hall and musical-comedy venue demolished in the 1950s.

clue.text: Possibly the Eye in short, neutral, got stuck into Maxwell, for example

parts.note: Private Eye is a magazine, shortened to mag
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear stick
to get stuck into food is to eat it heartily, so ate

explanation.surface: Private Eye joins the long campaign against the late press baron Robert Maxwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell was the newspaper owner Private Eye pursued for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Maxwell was a media tycoon, and a magnate is a wealthy, powerful businessman.

clue.text: Definitive sound dose?

parts.note: the is the definite article, so the definitive little word
a clap is a sharp sound, as of thunder or hands

explanation.surface: A query about the definitive dose of sound, as if prescribing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dose' is slang for a venereal infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a sexually transmitted infection; the clap is gonorrhoea, and to catch a dose means the same.

clue.text: Idealistic university to bump off editor!

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye

explanation.surface: A university planning to murder the magazine's editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopian scheme pictures a perfect society, which is an idealistic vision.

clue.text: What makes Di over-react? A vital statistic that's increasing?

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are what the answer's letters make when rearranged, so the phrase is jumbled to find it

explanation.surface: A question about what drove Princess Diana to overreact, linked to a rising figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is Princess Diana, whose divorce from Prince Charles was in the news; 'vital statistic' usually means body measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The proportion of marriages ending in divorce is a demographic figure that was rising.

clue.text: Bad image constraining good old PM?

indicators.note: the shuffled word holds the other letter in, so it goes inside
something bad is in poor shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A poor public image held back a once-good prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Maggie was the popular nickname of Margaret Thatcher, a former British prime minister.

clue.text: Lobbyist who apparently greased member (now out), of interest to one erstwhile feminist

definitions.text: Lobbyist who apparently greased member (now out), of interest to one erstwhile feminist

parts.words: Lobbyist who apparently greased member (now out), of interest to one erstwhile feminist
parts.note: the lobbyist in the 1990s cash-for-questions scandal, alleged to have paid an MP who later lost his seat, and who shares a surname with the feminist Germaine

explanation.surface: A lobbyist bribes an ousted MP, and an old feminist takes an interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Greer was accused of paying Neil Hamilton, who lost his seat in 1997; Germaine Greer is the feminist with the same surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Greer ran a parliamentary lobbying firm at the centre of the cash-for-questions affair.

clue.text: The Eye's so-called mobile toilet is not in office any more

definitions.text: The Eye's so-called mobile toilet is not in office any more

parts.words: The Eye's so-called mobile toilet is not in office any more
parts.note: Private Eye nicknamed this Conservative minister after a portable toilet brand, and he lost his seat in 1997

explanation.surface: A portable lavatory is no longer installed in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye called Michael Portillo 'Portaloo', a brand of portable toilet; he famously lost his Enfield seat in 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Portillo was a Conservative cabinet minister who was voted out of Parliament in the 1997 election.

clue.text: An easy catch, this outstanding songbird?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a ... is a very simple catch
second meaning: ... Parton, the country singer famous for her bust

explanation.surface: A prominent singing bird would be simple to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is a nod to Dolly Parton's figure; a dolly in cricket is a gentle catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket calls a gift of a catch a dolly, and Dolly Parton is the famous country singer.

clue.text: One and only Ginger possibly misses being the latest sensation

definitions.text: One and only Ginger possibly misses being the latest sensation

parts.words: One and only Ginger possibly misses being the latest sensation
parts.note: a 1990s pop group whose member nicknamed Ginger left, which the group might regret

explanation.surface: The unique Ginger is missing out on being the newest hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri Halliwell, Ginger Spice, quit the group in 1998; 'misses' is both regrets and lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spice Girls were the pop sensation of the late 1990s, and Ginger was one member's nickname.

clue.text: Correspondence of luvvies who've united to embrace Pacino

indicators.note: the union's name hugs the actor's first name, so it goes inside

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union; luvvies is slang for actors
Al Pacino, the American actor

explanation.surface: Actors joined in their union welcome Al Pacino into the fold.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean a match between things, and equality is sameness in amount or value.

clue.text: Big one — it's good, right, to admit it?

parts.note: to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: A large person is urged that it is good and proper to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call an adult a big one, a person who has grown up, which is the noun sense here.

clue.text: Mark: mug or public enemy?

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A mark on the face: is he a victim or a criminal?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' could be a dupe; here it is slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone, the gangster called Public Enemy Number One.

clue.text: Universal diet put about by a diabolical contractor

indicators.note: the fasting word is placed round the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: to fast is to go without food
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A universal diet promoted by a devilish dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: Faust is the legendary scholar who made a pact with the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Faust signed a contract with the Devil, so he is a party to a diabolical bargain.

clue.text: Describes an outmoded system of university in grip of Iron Lady (mad, youth gone)

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the university letter tight, so it goes inside

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: something mad is disordered, so these letters are jumbled
the youth letter has gone, so it is taken away

parts.note: taken as the word lady
Y is a standard abbreviation for youth, as in YMCA

explanation.surface: A university caught in the grip of a deranged Thatcher, her youth long behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' looks like Margaret Thatcher's nickname, but the two words work separately: a chemical symbol and a word to be shortened and jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was the medieval system of lords and vassals, long since obsolete, and feudal is its adjective.

clue.text: A top Tory leader right in the mire

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken from Tory
the letter for right sits inside the word for the mire

parts.note: slang for being in a mess, in the mire

explanation.surface: A senior Conservative, his party's leader, is right in the mire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A top' looks like a senior figure; it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shirt is a simple casual garment worn on the upper body, which is a top.

clue.text: Wild party clothes donned by cops getting in with a bad crowd?

definitions.text: donned by cops getting in with a bad crowd

parts.note: a riot is slang for a wild, raucous time
gear is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Clothes worn by undercover police mingling with a rough crowd at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of what police wear; 'getting in with a bad crowd' is facing a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Police wear protective helmets, shields and padding when tackling an unruly mob.

clue.text: Possibly off trolley, getting access to top grade university?

parts.note: a gate is a way in
A is the top grade in exams

explanation.surface: Someone off their trolley gets into a top university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off trolley' suggests madness; it means served from a dessert trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cream cake, the kind of dessert wheeled round restaurants on a trolley.

clue.text: Archer's tally of successes? Cobblers!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the number of bullseyes scored, with a dig at Jeffrey Archer
second meaning: British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer boasting of his successes is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is also the novelist Jeffrey Archer, whose claims Private Eye mocked; cobblers is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is vulgar slang for nonsense, and split in two it describes bullseyes scored by an archer.

clue.text: Tell someone in the event of being gobbled by new Tony

indicators.note: the jumbled name swallows the little word, so it goes inside
something made new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: if means in the event of

explanation.surface: A warning to inform someone if new Tony Blair swallows them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Tony' recalls Tony Blair's New Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify is to inform somebody formally of something.

clue.text: Good luck getting an easy lay as a teatime treat?

parts.note: jam is British slang for good luck, as in jammy
tart is slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A lucky man finds a willing partner over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam as luck gives the adjective jammy, meaning lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam tart is a small pastry filled with jam, served with afternoon tea.

clue.text: House news laid on thick by the Eye?

definitions.text: House news laid on thick by the Eye

parts.words: House news laid on thick by the Eye
parts.note: the name of Private Eye's column of parliamentary gossip, also a thick brown condiment

explanation.surface: Private Eye pours on the Westminster gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: HP stands for Houses of Parliament, and Private Eye's column of political gossip borrows the name of the brown sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: HP Sauce is a thick British brown sauce, and the Eye's Westminster column uses the same title.
